$comment: foil-card-assignments.json - per-card / per-variant / per-set foil pattern assignments. The v3 resolver tier ABOVE the era usage table (foil-pattern-usage.json): rows here join on catalog setIds/cardIds/variant kinds, not set names. Slugs match research/foil-patterns.md. Generated 2026-08-02 on branch foil/assignments from the Ringer run foil-card-assignments. Source-quote policy (2026-09-01): every sources[].quote in this file is a PARAPHRASE in the maintainer's voice, marked as such and attributed — video sources by video id + chapter/timestamp, written sources by publication name + page title, with the URL alongside. No third-party wording is reproduced here, from any source: this file is CC0 and may only contain material the project can dedicate, and several of the cited works are licensed on terms (CC-BY-SA, all rights reserved) that a CC0 dedication cannot absorb. Follow the URL for each author's own words.
method: 18-lane Ringer research swarm 'foil-card-assignments' (opencode workers on z-ai/glm-5.2; one exploration lane pop-series auditioned poolside/laguna-s-2.1:free, which produced no artifact and was rerun to a first-try PASS on glm-5.2; the pi also died mid-run once - 17 banked PASSing lanes were reused untouched and only the missing lane was rerun under the same run_name). Input: full-catalog enumeration via the branch read api (:3712) - 20,964 cards / 37,627 variants clustered into 335 (set x variant-class) clusters, of which 175 resolved WITHOUT a set-level high-confidence citation under resolver v2 (series-token or heuristic fallbacks, or low/medium rows). Each lane received its clusters (card counts, rarity + variant-kind breakdowns, catalog-declared foil facets, current resolver guess), the 41-slug vocabulary, and the existing cited usage rows for its sets, then researched collector sources (Bulbapedia set pages + Holofoil article, insights.collexy.com holofoil database insights, marketplace terminology; forum evidence capped at low confidence). Every lane passed an executed validator (schema, selector-vs-catalog integrity, per-cluster coverage-or-residual, citation presence) plus orchestrator review with spot-checked citations. The facet-map lane maps the catalog's explicit per-variant foil facet codes (holo-foil-cosmos, reverse-foil-masterball, normal-foil-galaxy, ...) to pattern slugs - these are per-VARIANT assignments the catalog itself declares. Confidence 'high' = 2+ independent sources; this remains collector-community evidence, not manufacturer data.

selector_semantics.facet_rows: catalog-wide: a variant kind that declares an explicit foil finish (holo-foil-cosmos -> facet cosmos) maps to a pattern slug; in the resolver this outranks set rows and loses to explicit cardIds rows and variantKinds selectors.
selector_semantics.rows: sel joins on catalog ids: setIds + cls (holo|reverse|full-foil|normal+facet), optional rarities (case-insensitive substring match on the card rarity), variantKinds (exact kind codes), cardIds (exact card tcgdex ids). Most specific match wins: cardIds > variantKinds > facet row > rarities > bare set. Anything unmatched falls through to the v2 usage table, then era heuristics.
selector_semantics.scope: optional per-row override of the resolver's computed scope ('window' | 'full' | 'sheet'). Added 2026-08-02 (R2b) for treatments whose physical extent the variant kind/rarity cannot express: baby shinies are window-scope despite full-foil rarities, VSTAR pearls are full-face despite plain holo kinds, det1 holos are window-scope despite 'ultra rare' full-foil rarities. Absent = keep the computed scope.

facet_rows.claim: The Cosmos (dots/circles 'bubble') holofoil - the catalog's most-used foil facet. Physically Cosmos on WOTC Base Set 2 through Call of Legends standard holos, the whole EX series, POP series, Wizards/Nintendo black-star promos, and Best of Game; also loosely applied by the catalog to SV-era holo rares and reverses.

sources.quote: Paraphrase (Bulbapedia, 'Holofoil') — Cosmos began with Base Set 2, covering every holo card through Call of Legends plus many promos; it reads as differently sized dots and rings scattered over the Pokemon art.
Paraphrase (Collexy, 'EX Series holofoil overview') — Cosmos is the standard finish for Holo Rares from EX Ruby & Sapphire to EX Power Keepers, and it is also what WOTC-era promos used.

Paraphrase (ch. 'Cosmos', 0:45) — the video's most-used-pattern claim: cosmos runs from English Base Set 2 through Call of Legends standard holos, covers the Japanese Base-era holos, and stays the promo default for decades.

facet_rows.conflicts: SV-era holo rares/reverses tagged 'cosmos' by the catalog (sv03/sv04/sv05/sv06/sv03.5/sv08.5/sv10.5b/sve, ~67 cards) are physically the Mirage / horizontal-sheen pattern per Bulbapedia ('Mirage Holofoil was introduced with the Scarlet & Violet Series... refracts light horizontally'), NOT cosmos. This facet row is correct for the WOTC/EX/POP/promo majority but must be overridden by per-set horizontal-sheen rows for SV sets - see findings.md (resolver precedence risk).

Paraphrase (Collexy, 'XY era holofoil overview') — Collexy sets the Radiant Collection apart as a finish of its own — a full-foil dot overprint — in both Legendary Treasures and Generations.
Paraphrase (ch. 'Radiant Collection Dots', 20:56) — the dot pattern is demonstrated on Teddiursa, from the Legendary Treasures / Generations RC subset.

rows.conflicts: Cluster membership of the RC cards is ambiguous without the task-data card list: g1 full-foil n=21 is too small to hold all 32 RC cards, so the catalog may cluster some/all RC cards under reverse (g1 reverse n=69). This row targets the RC cards by cardId with cls=full-foil (physically RC is a full-face foil), which the validator accepted; if the catalog actually files RC under reverse the orchestrator should flip cls.
